items.title: Elon Musk is the world's first trillionaire. Here's what that looks like
items.description: Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire. It is hard to fathom a figure so staggering, but let's give it a shot.

items.title: Abbott takes a 'hold your nose and accept the preferences' approach to One Nation
items.description: Tony Abbott has been back in the political cycle for barely a fortnight and already the air is redolent with garment-rending, ancient feuds, biblical comeuppance and a listening tour.

items.title: Both US and Iran signal peace deal is close
items.description: Mediator Pakistan says the text of a peace deal between the US and Iran has been "agreed".

items.title: Britain's defence strategy under fire while global nuclear spending surges
items.description: The prospect of nuclear weapons being used in either Ukraine or the Middle East, rather than being fired between Moscow, Washington or Beijing has risen.

items.title: The trait that defines Australia's 1.1 million power couples
items.description: The ranks of Australia's so-called power couples, in which both partners are university-educated, have almost quadrupled over 20 years. This could have profound implications for social inequality.

items.title: Live: Canada's World Cup party crashed by underdogs, Ghana star denied visa
items.description: World Cup co-host Canada gets its campaign underway in Toronto when it takes on Bosnia and Herzegovina. Follow live.

items.title: How far can the Socceroos really go at the FIFA World Cup?
items.description: This crop of Socceroos has been labelled the "next generation", but that doesn't mean they aren't aiming high at the FIFA World Cup.

items.title: Ivan Milat suspected in 11 additional murder, missing persons cases
items.description: A parliamentary inquiry has heard a police taskforce identified 11 unsolved homicide and missing persons cases with potential links to Ivan Milat.

items.title: David Hockney, giant of British art, dies aged 88
items.description: British artist David Hockney, whose paintings of pools shimmering in the Los Angeles sunshine became icons of 20th-century art, has died at the age of 88, his publicist has announced.

items.title: Billionaire says $150m court loss no reason to change approach to native title
items.description: Mining magnate Andrew "Twiggy" Forrest has defended his company's approach to Indigenous agreements after a court ordered the miner to pay $150 million in compensation to the Yindjibarndi people.

items.title: Gus Lamont's grandparent fined over gun offence, unrelated to 4yo's disappearance
items.description: The grandparent of missing four-year-old Gus Lamont has been fined $10,500 for possession of a gun silencer at the family's Oak Park Station, in South Australia's far north. Police have previously said the offence is not related to his disappearance.

items.title: What Australia would have looked like when the dinosaurs roamed
items.description: Palaeontologists say evidence pointing to Australia's polar past shows that many dinosaurs roamed the country when the south east was still within the Antarctic Circle.

items.title: Australian sprinter's death in Thailand came weeks after her 25th birthday
items.description: The brother of Stawell Gift finalist Jemma Stapleton remembers her "bright smile" and expresses gratitude for the outpouring of grief and support.

items.title: Two dead after Taliban opens fire on dress code violation protest
items.description: The protest followed the arrests of dozens of women for alleged dress code violation in the Afghan city of Herat.

items.title: Villages 700 years old destroyed to 'uproot people' from their history
items.description: Non-governmental organisations Biladi and Blue Shield are among the design experts using new technologies to create detailed records of cultural heritage and help rebuild after conflict.

items.title: ABC 50/50 quiz: Testing your knowledge of ABBA, the World Cup mascots and some fruity language
items.description: Each question in the ABC 50/50 quiz has only two options: one is right; the other is wrong. But there's a catch.

items.title: The big life lessons you've learnt since owning a pet
items.description: Pets can be lifelong companions, but they can also test us in ways we never imagined. We asked you to share your stories. Here's what you told us.

items.title: Parts of Australia on track for warmest start to winter on record
items.description: An influx of humid, tropical air has resulted in a remarkably warm and relatively wet start to winter across Australia.

items.title: 'Brighter' weekend forecast for Queensland despite some showers
items.description: Most Queenslanders are in for warmer and brighter weather this weekend, but scattered showers are expected to continue along parts of the coast.

items.title: Independence leader vanishes after changing sides to support Indonesia's government
items.description: A key Indigenous leader in West Papua appeared in a documentary criticising an Indonesian government program, but then changed sides and disappeared. Her family suspects foul play.

items.title: Senior Labor figures weigh in on BHP strike, cost could be $120m per day
items.description: Federal Resources Minister Madeleine King says workers threatening strike action at the nation's biggest port deserve "every single cent" of what they earn while a peak industry body says they are "letting down everyone".

items.title: What are the rules around using fire pits at home?
items.description: There are rules when it comes to using fire pits and things to be cautious about, including open-air fires being a nuisance to your neighbours.

items.title: Dolphins make it six on the trot with Rooster thrashing
items.description: The Dolphins have continued their march towards a maiden NRL finals appearance with a 48-10 trouncing of the Sydney Roosters at Lang Park.

items.title: Cats continue alarming Suns slide as Hardwick lashes 'ridiculous' rule
items.description: Geelong records a 45-point win over Gold Coast as Suns coach Damien Hardwick tees off at the officiating.

items.title: World Cup quick hits: Opening ceremony delights, drinks break drama and Haiti's jersey ban
items.description: The 2026 FIFA World Cup is up and running, launched by a colourful opening ceremony and comprehensive win for Mexico. Here are the quick hits from the opening day of the tournament.
